page: Amazon Web Services m8a.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It provides a single dedicated x86_64 vCPU powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz, backed by 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache. The CPU features instruction set extensions including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It includes no bundled local storage, no hardware GPUs, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-thread execution paired with throughput constraints typical of a single-core instance. In single-core evaluations, the server achieves top-tier results, registering 2795.0 in Geekbench single-core, 3762.69 in stress-ng single-core, and 41.2 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput tests like Geekbench multi-core (2784.0) and PassMark CPU (3490.66) fall into the lower quartile due to the absence of additional execution threads. Memory bandwidth achieves 47.43 GB/sec uncached read and 34.42 GB/sec write, facilitating moderate throughput for static web serving at 6.77 GB/sec and small 135M-parameter LLM prompt evaluation at 413.44 tokens/sec.

The absence of integrated local NVMe storage requires external volume attachments for persistent state, presenting an I/O consideration for disk-heavy processes. With dedicated single-core compute performance driven by high clock speeds, the instance offers efficient execution for latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks. Recommended workloads include microservices, lightweight web servers, background task runners, text and data processing scripts, and software development testing.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.medium is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with 1 dedicated vCPU on a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9R45 processor and 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture features advanced vector support, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and providing a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate exceptional single-threaded compute, ranking in the top decile for single-core Geekbench, stress-ng, and single-threaded gzip compression. However, its overall capacity is constrained by the single-thread execution model, resulting in bottom-quartile multi-core and database transaction scores. Memory bandwidth achieves moderate throughput, clocking 47.43 GB/sec read. The m8a.medium is appropriate for lightweight microservices, single-threaded batch processing, utility servers, and development tasks requiring modern CPU features without multi-threaded concurrency.
